manifest.name: Newsletter Subscribe Button
manifest.summary: Attract visitors to subscribe to mailing lists

models._description: (inherit-only) _get_social_media_links override so the newsletter/footer social links fall back to the current website's social_* fields

routes.note: website=True; returns {is_subscriber, value} for the current visitor against a mailing.list by counting non-opted-out mailing.subscription rows; pre-fills + disables the snippet when already subscribed
website=True; recaptcha-gated newsletter opt-in -- find-or-create mailing.contact + mailing.subscription on the target list (or clear opt_out), returns a success/danger toast

security.note: Single ir.model.access (access_mailing_list_website_designer) grants read-only on mass_mailing.mailing.list to website.group_website_designer (so a designer can pick the list when configuring the snippet). The public subscribe/is_subscriber routes themselves run sudo() on mailing.subscription / mailing.contact; no own record rules or groups.

views.note: No backend data views of its own. 466 XML LOC are website snippet templates: the newsletter subscribe inline block, the newsletter popup, the benefits popup (static/shapes/s_newsletter_benefits_popup.svg) and website-builder option panels (list picker, layout, recaptcha toggle). The single 'form' is the website form-editor binding for create_mailing_contact.

behavioral_notes.observation: This is the snippet's opt-in endpoint and overrides nothing -- it is a new route on the inherited mass_mailing.controllers.main.MassMailController. It FIRST calls request.env['ir.http']._verify_request_recaptcha_token('website_mass_mailing_subscribe'); if that raises UserError it returns early with {'toast_type':'danger','toast_content': str(e)} and never touches the data -- so the recaptcha is a hard gate on the whole subscription, unlike website_mail where the captcha only gates partner creation. On success it derives fname via _get_fname(subscription_type) ('email' for the 'email' type, '' otherwise) and calls the static subscribe_to_newsletter(subscription_type, value, list_id, fname), then returns {'toast_type':'success','toast_content': 'Thanks for subscribing!'}. The toast strings are exactly what the Subscribe public.interaction renders via the notification service.

The core side-effect, all sudo(). For an 'email' subscription it parses name/value out of the raw input via tools.parse_contact_from_email(value) (so 'Joe <joe@x.com>' is split). It then searches mailing.subscription for an existing row on (list_id, contact_id.<fname> == value) limit 1. THREE branches: (a) no subscription AND no mailing.contact with that value -> create the mailing.contact({name, fname:value}) then create the mailing.subscription({contact_id, list_id}); (b) no subscription but a contact already exists -> reuse it and only create the mailing.subscription; (c) a subscription already exists and is opted-out -> flip subscription.opt_out = False (re-subscribe); (d) an active subscription -> no-op. Finally it writes request.session['mass_mailing_<fname>'] = value so the visitor's email is remembered for is_subscriber on later page loads. Net: a website visitor self-creates a mailing.contact and joins a mailing.list, idempotently, without login.

Decides whether to show the snippet as 'already subscribed'. _get_value(subscription_type) resolves the visitor's email WITHOUT a form: a logged-in user -> request.env.user.email; a public user -> request.session.get('mass_mailing_email') if a prior subscribe stored it (else None). Only when both value and fname are truthy does it sudo().search_count mailing.subscription on (list_id in [list_id], contact_id.<fname> == value, opt_out == False); is_subscriber = count > 0. Returns {'is_subscriber', 'value'} -- value is echoed back so the snippet can pre-fill the email box and disable the button. opt_out is part of the predicate, so an opted-out contact correctly shows as NOT subscribed and can re-join.

behavioral_notes.element: WebsiteNewsletterForm._handle_website_form (controllers/website_form.py) -> private-list guard on the generic website form path
behavioral_notes.observation: Beyond the two jsonrpc routes, the module also extends website.controllers.form.WebsiteForm: when the generic website Form snippet posts model_name=='mailing.contact', _handle_website_form requires a list_ids param (else {'error':'Mailing List(s) not found!'}), splits it to ints, and sudo()-searches mailing.list for any of those that are is_public=False; if found it refuses with 'You cannot subscribe to the following list anymore : <names>'. Only then does it super(). This is the security boundary that stops a crafted form POST from enrolling visitors into private/internal mailing lists -- the create_mailing_contact form action is whitelisted to public lists only. Invisible to metadata.

The only model override: _get_social_media_links() super-extends the company social link dict and overlays the CURRENT website's social_facebook / social_linkedin / social_twitter / social_instagram / social_tiktok (via website.get_current_website()) when set, falling back to the company values otherwise. This makes the newsletter block / footer social icons multi-website aware (each website can advertise its own social handles). Pure read-side computation, no persistence.

behavioral_notes.element: frontend (OWL/JS newsletter snippet + popup) -- metadata gap #3
behavioral_notes.observation: Copied intent from frontend/website_mass_mailing.frontend.json: present=true, 13 JS files, 5 XML templates, 0 OWL components, registry_adds ['public.interactions.edit:website_mass_mailing.fix_newsletter_list_class','public.interactions:website_mass_mailing.subscribe','website.form_editor_actions:create_mailing_contact'], patches ['FormOptionPlugin.prototype','Popup.prototype'], services ['email','list_ids','name'], bundles {web.assets_frontend:5, website.website_builder_assets:4, website.assets_inside_builder_iframe:1, web.assets_tests:1, web.assets_unit_tests:1, web.assets_unit_tests_setup:1}. The Subscribe public.interaction (static/src/interactions/subscribe.js, selector .js_subscribe) on load RPCs /is_subscriber to toggle subscribe-vs-subscribed UI, validates the email regex, loads google_recaptcha (and renders a Cloudflare turnstile widget when session.turnstile_site_key is set), then RPCs /subscribe with list_id/value/subscription_type/token and shows the returned toast; on success it disables the form and hides the enclosing .o_newsletter_modal. The Popup.prototype patch (popup.js) suppresses the newsletter popup (canShowPopup=false) when the visitor is already subscribed, and stops the subscribe button from closing the popup prematurely. The remaining JS is website-builder option UI (list picker, layout, recaptcha toggle, form editor). All interactive behavior lives in static/src.

it_architecture.application: website_mass_mailing (Newsletter Subscribe Button -- website snippet/popup that enrolls visitors into Email-Marketing mailing lists)
software_services: /website_mass_mailing/subscribe (jsonrpc, public, website: recaptcha-gated find-or-create mailing.contact + mailing.subscription on a list; toast response)
/website_mass_mailing/is_subscriber (jsonrpc, public, website: report whether the current visitor already subscribes to a list, echo their email)
WebsiteNewsletterForm._handle_website_form (extends the generic website Form controller to block private-list enrollment for create_mailing_contact)
logical_data_erm: mailing.subscription -> mailing.contact (contact_id) + mailing.list (list_id) with opt_out flag
request.session['mass_mailing_email'] -> remembered visitor email for is_subscriber
information_flows: side-effect: POST /website_mass_mailing/subscribe -> recaptcha 'website_mass_mailing_subscribe' (hard gate) -> subscribe_to_newsletter -> find-or-create mailing.contact + mailing.subscription / clear opt_out -> session email stored -> success toast
flow: POST /website_mass_mailing/is_subscriber -> mailing.subscription.search_count(opt_out=False) -> snippet shows subscribed vs subscribe
guard: generic website Form POST (mailing.contact) -> _handle_website_form rejects private (is_public=False) lists
side-effect: res.company._get_social_media_links -> overlay current website social_* handles
frontend_components: Subscribe (public.interaction: is_subscriber load, email validation, recaptcha+turnstile, subscribe RPC, toast, modal close)
Popup.prototype (patch: hide newsletter popup when already subscribed; keep popup open on subscribe click)
FormOptionPlugin.prototype + create_mailing_contact (website form-editor action wiring the Form snippet to mailing.contact)
fix_newsletter_list_class (edit-mode public.interaction normalizing the snippet's list-id markup)

external_integrations.notes: No own outbound HTTP/SDK/API keys. google_recaptcha verifies the subscribe token server-side; an optional Cloudflare turnstile widget renders client-side when session.turnstile_site_key is configured. All data coupling is internal Odoo (mass_mailing subscription/contact/list, website current-website + form controller).

capabilities: Website Newsletter Opt-in (self-service subscribe to a mailing list from a snippet/popup)
Find-or-Create Web Contacts into Mailing Lists (mailing.contact + mailing.subscription)
Re-subscribe / Opt-out-aware Enrollment (clear opt_out, never double-subscribe)
Show Already-Subscribed State to Returning Visitors (session + is_subscriber)
Spam-protected Subscription (recaptcha + optional Cloudflare turnstile gate)
Private-List Protection on the Generic Website Form
value_streams: Visitor-to-Subscriber: visitor sees newsletter block/popup -> enters email -> passes recaptcha -> mailing.contact found/created + mailing.subscription added (or opt_out cleared) on the chosen list -> email remembered in session -> returning visitor sees 'subscribed' state -> contact is now reachable by Email Marketing campaigns to that list
organization: website.group_website_designer (read-only on mailing.list, to configure the snippet)
policies: recaptcha 'website_mass_mailing_subscribe' must pass before any contact/subscription is created (hard gate)
Idempotent enrollment: existing active subscription -> no-op; opted-out -> opt_out cleared; missing -> create
Generic website Form may only enroll into is_public=True mailing lists (private lists rejected by _handle_website_form)
is_subscriber counts only non-opted-out subscriptions (opted-out visitors can re-join)
Public routes act sudo() on mailing.subscription/contact after the captcha gate
stakeholders: Website visitor (newsletter subscriber, anonymous or logged-in)
Website designer (configures the snippet, picks the mailing list)
Marketing user (consumes the grown mailing.list for campaigns via mass_mailing)
Mailing list / audience (mailing.list the contact is added to)
metrics: subscriptions created per list (mailing.subscription rows, opt_out=False)
is_subscriber conversion signal (returning visitors shown subscribed)
mailing.list contact counts feeding campaign reach (from mass_mailing)

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: website_mass_mailing is the website-side audience-acquisition front-end of the mass_mailing value network (which is itself network / 3.0 in this corpus): it is mediating-technology that connects an open population of anonymous web visitors to the firm's mailing lists by self-service opt-in, find-or-creating a mailing.contact and a mailing.subscription on each subscribe. Per Stabell & Fjeldstad the value is network promotion & contract management -- recruiting and enrolling participants into the contact network -- and its worth grows with the number of subscribers captured, not via a sequential transformation (chain) or a diagnostic problem-solving cycle (shop). activity_class is primary because the newsletter snippet is a demand-side lead/audience-capture service the public website delivers (it directly grows the marketable audience), not a back-office support function. apqc_category 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services (3.4 Develop and manage marketing communications -- subscriber/lead capture for the email channel) fits because the artifact converts website traffic into opted-in marketing contacts, mirroring website_mail, website_links and mass_mailing in this set. The recaptcha/turnstile gate and private-list guard are compliance/anti-abuse policies on that capture, not a separate value model.

standard_capabilities: Drop-in 'Newsletter' inline block and 'Newsletter Popup' website snippets bound to a chosen mailing.list
One-click public subscribe -> find-or-create mailing.contact + mailing.subscription (or clear opt_out)
recaptcha v3 + optional Cloudflare turnstile spam protection on subscribe
Already-subscribed detection (session email + is_subscriber) that pre-fills/disables the form and suppresses the popup
Website Form-snippet 'create_mailing_contact' action with private-list protection
Multi-website social links fallback on the newsletter/footer block
Website-builder options to pick the list, layout, and toggle recaptcha
typical_fits: Newsletter sign-up block in a page footer or hero section
Exit-intent / timed newsletter popup growing a marketing list
Lead capture funneling website visitors into an Email Marketing audience
Multi-site setups where each website feeds its own mailing list and shows its own social handles
common_gaps: No double opt-in / confirmation email -- a subscribe (post captcha) joins the list immediately
Only email (and a generic 'mobile' value placeholder) subscription types out of box; richer profile fields need the generic Form snippet
Anonymous already-subscribed detection is session-bound (cleared session shows the form again)
Unsubscribe is not on this snippet -- handled by mass_mailing's unsubscribe pages
List must be configured by a website designer; no per-visitor list self-selection beyond what the designer exposes

odoo shell: env['mailing.contact'].search([('email','=','visitor@example.com')]).subscription_list_ids  # lists a web-captured contact joined

Whether google_recaptcha and/or website_cf_turnstile are configured in the target deployment -- the subscribe route hard-fails the opt-in if recaptcha is enabled but the token is invalid.
